from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Planar graphs have no crossing edges.", 
                         "Identify vertices, edges, and faces.", 
                         "Faces include the infinite outer region.", 
                         "A house graph has five vertices.", 
                         "It has six edges, two faces."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph", lecture_lines)
        
        # Build the "house" graph
        # Vertices (5)
        # B2: peak, C1, C3: wall top, D1, D3: base
        nodes = {
            "p": Dot(color=WHITE),
            "tl": Dot(color=WHITE),
            "tr": Dot(color=WHITE),
            "bl": Dot(color=WHITE),
            "br": Dot(color=WHITE)
        }
        pos = {
            "p": "B3",
            "tl": "C2",
            "tr": "C4",
            "bl": "D2",
            "br": "D4"
        }
        for k, v in nodes.items():
            self.place_at_grid(v, pos[k])
        
        # Edges (6)
        edges = VGroup(
            Line(nodes["p"].get_center(), nodes["tl"].get_center(), color=WHITE),
            Line(nodes["p"].get_center(), nodes["tr"].get_center(), color=WHITE),
            Line(nodes["tl"].get_center(), nodes["tr"].get_center(), color=WHITE),
            Line(nodes["tl"].get_center(), nodes["bl"].get_center(), color=WHITE),
            Line(nodes["tr"].get_center(), nodes["br"].get_center(), color=WHITE),
            Line(nodes["bl"].get_center(), nodes["br"].get_center(), color=WHITE)
        )
        
        graph = VGroup(edges, *nodes.values())

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(graph))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(nodes["p"].animate.set_color("#FF0000"),
                  nodes["tl"].animate.set_color("#FF0000"),
                  nodes["tr"].animate.set_color("#FF0000"),
                  nodes["bl"].animate.set_color("#FF0000"),
                  nodes["br"].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(edges.animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        face_rect = Polygon(nodes["tl"].get_center(), nodes["tr"].get_center(), nodes["br"].get_center(), nodes["bl"].get_center(), 
                           fill_opacity=0.3, color="#0000FF", stroke_width=0)
        self.play(FadeIn(face_rect))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#0000FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        text_prop = Text("V=5, E=6, F=2", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(text_prop, "E3")
        self.play(Write(text_prop))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Concept of Duality", [
            "Define the Dual Graph, G-star.",
            "Place a vertex in each face.",
            "Connect dual vertices sharing an edge."
        ])
        
        # Original Graph (Simple Cycle/Grid-like)
        g = VGroup(
            Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B4"]),
            Line(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["D4"]),
            Line(self.grid["D4"], self.grid["D2"]),
            Line(self.grid["D2"], self.grid["B2"]),
            Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["D2"]),
            Line(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["D4"])
        ).set_stroke(WHITE, 2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(g))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # Dual Vertices
        dual_v1 = Dot(self.grid["C3"], color="#FFFF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(dual_v1))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Dual Edges
        # Since this is a simple 1-face graph inside a boundary, 
        # showing duality conceptually:
        dual_e1 = Line(self.grid["C3"], self.grid["C3"]).set_stroke("#00FFFF", 3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(dual_e1))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Interplay of Duality and Euler", ["Dual vertices map to original faces.", "Edges remain the same in number.", "Faces become vertices in the dual."])
        
        # Create a simple triangle graph (original G)
        v1 = Dot(self.grid["B3"], color=BLUE)
        v2 = Dot(self.grid["D2"], color=BLUE)
        v3 = Dot(self.grid["D4"], color=BLUE)
        e1 = Line(v1.get_center(), v2.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e2 = Line(v2.get_center(), v3.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e3 = Line(v3.get_center(), v1.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        graph = VGroup(e1, e2, e3, v1, v2, v3)
        self.add(graph)
        
        # Create a dual vertex in the center of the triangle
        dual_v = Dot(self.grid["C3"], color=YELLOW)
        dual_graph = VGroup(dual_v)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(dual_graph))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Indicate edge mapping (no change in number, just highlight)
        edge_label = Text("E = E*", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(edge_label, "E3")
        self.play(Write(edge_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        face_label = Text("F = V*", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(face_label, "F3")
        self.play(Write(face_label))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Unlocking Planar Graphs: Euler's Characteristic and Duality

sections.title: Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph
sections.content: Define a planar graph as one that can be drawn in a 2D plane without edges crossing. Introduce the basic components: Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Faces (F), where a 'face' is an enclosed region (including the infinite outer region).
sections.example: Visualizing a house shape: 5 vertices (the house outline + roof peak), 6 edges, and 2 faces (the interior and the exterior).

sections.title: The Master Equation: Euler's Characteristic
sections.content: Introduce Euler's formula: V - E + F = 2. Explain how this fundamental invariant holds true for any connected planar graph regardless of how messy the layout looks, provided no edges cross.
sections.example: Apply the formula to a simple triangle: V=3, E=3, F=2. Calculation: 3 - 3 + 2 = 2. It holds!

sections.title: Concept of Duality
sections.content: Introduce the Dual Graph (G*). To create a dual, place a point (vertex) inside each face of the original graph and connect two points if their corresponding faces share an edge.
sections.example: Visualize a 'Grid City'. Each city block is a face. By placing a park in the center of each block and connecting parks across streets, you create the 'Dual Park Network'.

sections.title: Interplay of Duality and Euler
sections.content: Show how duality maps components: The number of faces in the original graph becomes the number of vertices in the dual (F=V*). The edges remain the same (E=E*).
sections.example: An animation showing a 'Triangle Graph' transforming into its dual 'Y-shaped Graph', highlighting how the central vertex of the dual corresponds to the outer face of the original.

sections.title: Application and Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize the utility of duality in circuit design and map coloring proofs. Reiterate that these tools allow us to simplify complex networks by viewing them through their dual 'mirrors'.
sections.example: Imagine a drone delivery robot navigating a complex web of roads; it uses the dual graph to find the shortest 'corridor' path between the centers of city blocks.
